title: Natun Puhorat Asamiya Sahityar Buranji
author: Prof. Dimbeshwar Neog
genre: Critical Literary History & Chronicle of Assam's Linguistic Traditions
description: Monumental sixth revised edition of Prof. Dimbeshwar Neog's masterly literary history of Assam, providing authoritative analysis of the early Tai-Ahom chronicling traditions (Buranji literature), folk ballads, early bilingual inscriptions, Vaisnavite narrative texts, and the interaction between Tai Khamyang, Ahom, and Assamese prose.

sentences.free_translation_en: The literary history of Assam is an invaluable treasure providing illumination to human knowledge.

sentences.free_translation_en: The Ahom monarchs instituted an exceptional tradition of systematic historical record-keeping termed Buranji.

sentences.speaker: Literary Historian
sentences.notes: Chapter on the Tai-Ahom Buranji prose legacy.

sentences.text_roman: pu ran kyi pen kwam lik an taem loy lawng tae am mi khaw mu sa

sentences.free_translation_en: A Buranji is a factual prose narrative composed with strict fidelity to empirical truth without exaggeration.
sentences.free_translation_as: বুৰঞ্জী হৈছে নিৰপেক্ষ আৰু বাস্তৱনিষ্ঠ গদ্য ৰূপ, য'ত কোনো অত্যুক্তি বা অসত্যৰ ঠাই নাই।
sentences.speaker: Prof. Dimbeshwar Neog
sentences.notes: Defining the historiographical rigor of Tai chronicles.

sentences.free_translation_en: The Ahom bark manuscripts represent some of the earliest continuous secular prose in eastern India.
